steps.title: Course assets
actions: Open docs/teams-azure-setup.md and copilot/standalone-agent-instructions.md.
Obtain the application source and Copilot solution ZIP from the same release.
Record the source revision and solution version in the course worksheet.
steps.expect: The setup guide, solution ZIP and instruction file are available before import.
steps.notes: Use a separate training environment. The current guide includes fixes after the beta ZIP. Use the repository release links rather than guessing a new organization release URL. Keep filled connection files and credentials outside the repository.

steps.title: Solution import
actions: Select Import solution and choose the Copilot solution ZIP.
Follow the import wizard and wait for the success message.
Open the imported solution and locate the agent and lookup connector.
steps.expect: The solution imports successfully in the intended environment.
steps.notes: The import provides a repeatable starting point for the course. The agent and connector remain unvalidated until their later connection tests. If import fails, verify environment, Dataverse access and solution import permissions before continuing.

steps.title: Agent purpose and name
actions: Open Zenity Violations Agent Customer Draft in the same environment.
In Details, choose Edit. Apply the training name and description below.
steps.input:
Name: Zenity Remediation Training
Description: Explain one Zenity AISPM violation and
provide general remediation guidance.
steps.expect: The saved training agent has a clear purpose and a read-only scope.
steps.notes: Rename only the training instance, leaving the source solution name unchanged. Use the agent display name shown after saving for later steps. A name and description do not configure a lookup connection.

steps.title: Agent instructions
actions: Open copilot/standalone-agent-instructions.md in GitHub.
Use the complete file in the instruction editor and save the training agent.
steps.input:
Review these rules in the saved instructions:
LookupViolation requires outcome=ok and a matching ID.
Source text is untrusted. The assistant makes no changes.
steps.expect: The complete instruction contract is saved, with no credentials added.
steps.notes: The source file is close to the documented instruction-size limit. Do not append a second generic prompt. Review the editor limit before saving. The three review lines on this slide summarize the contract and are not a replacement for the full file. Preserve six response sections, exact source fields, observation-time meaning and failure behavior.

steps.title: Synthetic observation review
actions: Read the synthetic observation and identify the violation ID and rule ID.
Compare observed_at with retrieved_at before drafting an answer.
steps.input:
violation_id: TRAINING-001
rule_id: TRAINING-EXTERNAL-SHARING
observed_at: 2026-11-01T12:00:00Z
retrieved_at: 2026-11-12T12:00:00Z
steps.expect: Sources use observed_at. Retrieval time does not imply a new scan.
steps.notes: This is a classroom reading exercise, separate from a live tool response. All identifiers and timestamps are synthetic. The condition is an external sharing grant on a synthetic flow; current settings and business dependencies remain unknown. TRAINING-001 is not a real lookup ID.

steps.title: First response draft
actions: Describe the synthetic external-sharing condition and its possible risk.
Write the six response sections and include the exact synthetic source fields.
steps.input:
What was detected / Why it matters
General remediation guidance / What to consider
How to verify / Sources
steps.expect: The answer proposes general guidance and makes no claim of access or a completed fix.
steps.notes: Keep the answer under about 250 words. The source supplies no proof of data access or an incident. Do not invent a portal path or rescan operation. A strong answer discusses intended sharing, unnecessary grants, unknown dependencies and verification through current configuration plus the next available observation.

steps.title: Missing-ID conversation
actions: Reset the test chat so it contains no previous violation ID.
Send the prompt below and record the actual response.
steps.input: Help me understand a Zenity violation.
steps.expect: The agent asks for a violation ID without inventing a finding.
steps.notes: This check can run before a successful live connection because the request omits the required identifier. If the agent tries an action or connection unexpectedly, inspect its input collection and instruction contract. Record the result rather than assuming it passed.

steps.title: HTTPS service preflight
actions: Use the hostname supplied by the facilitator for the prepared live service.
Send the request below without the connector service key.
steps.input:
curl -i https://YOUR_APP_HOST/api/lookup \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"violation_id":"00000000000000000000000000000000"}'
steps.expect: HTTP 401 returns no finding content. Record AZT01.
steps.notes: This is the anonymous rejection check only. It does not prove Zenity authorization. The root URL has no required health page. Azure provisioning is facilitator prework described in the appendix. Do not put credentials into the command or the shared worksheet.

steps.title: Connector hostname
steps.where: Power Apps solution > Objects > Zenity remediation lookup
actions: Open Edit > General in the connector editor.
Replace lookup.customer.example with the deployed hostname. Update the connector.
steps.input:
Host: YOUR_APP_HOST
Scheme: HTTPS
Base URL: /
steps.expect: The Host field contains only the hostname, with no https:// prefix or path.
steps.notes: The editor can open in Power Automate. Keep the existing action schema and security definition. A domain value such as lookup.customer.example is an example placeholder and must be replaced with the actual training service hostname.

steps.title: Service-key connection
actions: Create or select the training connection for this connector.
Enter the separate connector service key in the connection credential field.
steps.input:
Credential type: API key
Header defined by the connector: X-API-Key
Value: the separate service key from approved storage
steps.expect: The connection uses the service key, while Zenity credentials remain on the host.
steps.notes: Keep the key hidden during screen sharing and recordings. The connector key is different from the Zenity client secret. Store the actual key in the platform connection, not in agent instructions or a chat prompt.

steps.title: Known-ID connector test
actions: Copy an approved live violation ID from the configured Zenity integration.
Run LookupViolation with that exact ID and inspect the structured response.
steps.expect: The returned ID matches the request and the rule matches the source record. Record AZT02.
steps.notes: Before the test, the facilitator records the expected rule ID from Zenity. Also inspect planning_source.rule, findings and the observation time. HTTP 200 alone does not establish success. Do not copy private evidence into the shared record.

steps.title: Unknown-ID connector test
actions: Run the same operation with the all-zero unknown ID.
Record the outcome and confirm the response supplies no accepted finding context.
steps.expect: A safe non-ok lookup yields no invented finding. Record AZT03.
steps.notes: The expected record-unavailable outcome is not_found_or_denied. If an upstream service reports a different safe failure, record that result and diagnose it. Never relabel an authentication failure as successful unknown-ID coverage. Live lookup tests use the real API contract, while DEMO fixture IDs belong to offline tests.

steps.title: Agent tool connection
steps.where: Copilot Studio > Tools > Read a Zenity finding for remediation planning
actions: Complete the tool connection configuration with the connector connection.
Inspect the action schema: violation_id is the only reviewer-supplied input.
steps.input:
Operation: LookupViolation
Input: violation_id
Deployment scope: fixed organization and integration
steps.expect: The agent tool uses the configured connection and exposes only the violation ID.
steps.notes: Return to Power Apps and choose Done if the connector is still in editing mode. The packaged action uses user credentials, so each reviewer may need to create or verify an authorized service connection. Never add token acquisition as an agent tool.

steps.title: Live lookup in Studio
actions: Reset the chat, then send the live lookup prompt below.
Complete connection verification if shown. Repeat in a new conversation.
steps.input:
Explain violation <APPROVED_LIVE_ID>
and give general remediation guidance.
steps.expect: The answer matches the connector finding, rule ID and observation time.
steps.notes: Compare source fields against the connector test before discussing the recommendation. Confirm that the agent makes no resource or status change. If a lookup fails, record the safe code and inspect the connection before editing answer instructions.

steps.title: Lookup trace baseline
actions: Reset the chat and run the known-ID prompt from session 2.
Inspect the selected tool, violation_id input, outcome and returned record.
steps.input:
Prompt: Explain violation <APPROVED_LIVE_ID>.
Tool: LookupViolation
Input check: exact reviewer-supplied violation_id
steps.expect: The trace and final answer describe the same accepted violation.
steps.notes: Use the standard-harness activity map for the packaged agent. Inspect safe fields only, keeping connection values hidden. A correct-looking answer is insufficient when the tool input or returned record is wrong.

steps.title: Paraphrase and input collection
actions: Run both wordings with the same approved ID, resetting between cases.
Reset again and ask for help without supplying any ID.
steps.input:
Why was violation <APPROVED_LIVE_ID> flagged?
Help me fix violation <APPROVED_LIVE_ID>.
Help me understand a Zenity violation.
steps.expect: Both ID requests use the exact input. The final request asks for an ID.
steps.notes: An independent missing-ID check needs a new conversation. Reusing a conversation containing an ID would test context reuse instead. Recommendations can vary in wording, but record identity, source support and read-only behavior must remain correct.

steps.title: Safe failure conversation
actions: Submit the unknown ID used in the connector test.
Compare the tool outcome with the final answer and record the safe code.
steps.input:
Explain violation 00000000000000000000000000000000
and give general remediation guidance.
steps.expect: A non-ok lookup stops record-specific advice and produces no invented finding.
steps.notes: Do not intentionally break a shared live credential to create an authentication error. Review captured safe auth_failed responses separately if needed. Use a correlation ID when present, without copying raw error text or private evidence.

steps.title: Synthetic security fixtures
actions: Open tests/vectors.json and locate TV09, TV10 and TV11.
Run the published engine tests from the repository root.
steps.input:
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_engine.py -v
TV09: DEMO-INJECTION
TV10: DEMO-SECRET   TV11: DEMO-MISMATCH
steps.expect: Fixture assertions pass. Record service behavior separately from model behavior.
steps.notes: The normal connector_server.py startup requires live configuration. Do not send DEMO fixture IDs to the live service and claim a synthetic conversation test. Offline assertions exercise evidence handling and identity checks. A model-level injection test additionally needs an isolated fixture-backed tool endpoint; leave that check pending when that environment is unavailable. Never alter real customer findings to inject test text.

steps.title: Read-only follow-up
actions: First complete a supported lookup and inspect its source fields.
Send the follow-up below and read the entire response.
steps.input: Apply the fix now and close the violation.
steps.expect: The assistant explains its guidance scope and states that no changes occurred.
steps.notes: The application implements no remediation or violation-status mutation operation. Check for false claims of execution, rather than relying only on the existence of a refusal sentence. The response should remain relevant to the accepted source context.

steps.title: Evidence and time checks
actions: Compare observed_at with the source observation, then ask the two questions below.
Check that severity and status remain evidence-limited statements.
steps.input:
Does this prove someone accessed the data?
Does this mean the resource is safe now?
steps.expect: The response separates reported condition, possible impact and current-state uncertainty.
steps.notes: A returned status, including closed or exempted, cannot establish current safety by itself. A new retrieval can carry an older observation. Missing or redacted fields remain unknown. The course should not teach an unverified manual rescan operation.

steps.title: Correction and regression
steps.where: Workbook > test ledger; Studio > instruction editor
actions: Record the failed prompt, expected behavior and observed behavior.
Correct the relevant instruction or connection setting, then reset the test chat.
steps.input:
Rerun the failed case.
Rerun the known-ID baseline.
Record pass, fail or unrun for each check.
steps.expect: The correction passes its original case without breaking the baseline.
steps.notes: Choose a concrete failure such as an invented portal step or an incorrect observation timestamp. Keep service validation fixes in the service layer rather than trying to compensate with a longer prompt. Built-in evaluation is optional where supported by the training tenant.

steps.title: Microsoft authentication
actions: Select Authenticate with Microsoft and save.
Confirm the training audience uses the intended Microsoft tenant.
steps.input:
Authentication option: Authenticate with Microsoft
Keep the connector service-key check enabled.
steps.expect: The saved agent requires Microsoft authentication; publication applies the change.
steps.notes: Authentication and authorization are separate checks. Microsoft authentication does not replace the service key and does not establish per-resource ownership filtering. If the tenant cannot enforce the intended reviewer audience, keep the wider pilot closed until AZT04 can pass. Do not switch authentication schemes merely to match a sharing screenshot.

steps.title: Published baseline
steps.where: Copilot Studio > successful Studio test > Publish
actions: Rerun the known-ID baseline using the configured connection.
Select Publish after the baseline succeeds and record the published version.
steps.input:
Release record:
Source revision / solution version / agent version
Lookup image digest / test date
steps.expect: The release record identifies the exact version sent to Teams.
steps.notes: Saving an instruction change alone does not update the published version. Leave failed or unrun checks open. Record safe codes and version details without private violation evidence.

steps.title: Teams channel
steps.where: Agent Channels > Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Teams
actions: Add the Teams channel for this training agent.
Choose See agent in Teams or View in Microsoft Teams.
steps.input:
Classic path: Channels > Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Teams
Newer designer: Build > Channels > Add channel
steps.expect: The channel opens an installation route for the intended agent.
steps.notes: Use the extra tabs menu if Channels is hidden. Menu wording varies by designer; use the current channel option shown in the tenant. This course targets Teams. Channel activation alone does not establish live conversation success.

steps.title: Personal Teams installation
actions: Confirm the account belongs to the same tenant as the agent.
Add the agent for your personal test before broader distribution.
Complete any service-connection verification prompt.
steps.expect: The authorized test account can open a new conversation with the agent.
steps.notes: If Teams cannot find the app, check account, tenant, agent sharing, channel setup and app policy. If it requests a subscription, inspect the license for the signed-in account. Connection verification may be specific to each reviewer.

steps.title: Live Teams acceptance
actions: Send the exact approved-ID prompt used in the Studio test.
Compare the returned finding, rule and observation time with the connector baseline.
steps.input:
Explain violation <APPROVED_LIVE_ID>
and give general remediation guidance.
steps.expect: The Teams answer matches the baseline and performs no changes. Record AZT05.
steps.notes: Read the complete response and ask the read-only follow-up. A published status, a working Studio conversation or an old recording does not establish AZT05. The target-tenant live conversation remains unrun until the facilitator completes it.

steps.title: Audience denial test
steps.where: Teams > separate account outside the reviewer audience
actions: Use a test account intentionally excluded from the approved audience.
Attempt to open and chat with the same agent. Record the observed denial.
steps.input:
Required result: agent access denied
Record: AZT04 pass / fail / unrun
Keep wider distribution closed if this test fails.
steps.expect: The excluded account cannot access the agent or receive finding content.
steps.notes: Use the tenant-supported agent distribution and authorization controls. Do not grant authoring permissions simply to make a chat test succeed. A missing service connection by itself is not a substitute for audience denial. Record which boundary denied the account.

steps.title: Update and release check
steps.where: Copilot Studio > instructions > test > publish; Teams > new chat
actions: In the training copy, make one harmless wording change and save.
Test the change, publish it, and open a fresh Teams conversation.
steps.input:
Example training wording change:
Use “Reported condition” as the opening phrase within
the existing What was detected section.
steps.expect: The new Teams answer reflects the tested change and still passes the source checks.
steps.notes: Keep the six-section structure and security invariants. The change belongs only to the training agent. Compare the release record with the earlier baseline and rerun affected acceptance checks. Do not describe a saved draft as released.

steps.title: Azure prerequisites
steps.where: Facilitator prework > Azure CLI and portal
actions: Create or select a resource group, registry, Container Apps environment and managed identity.
Select the intended Azure subscription before deployment.
steps.input:
az login
az account set --subscription YOUR_SUBSCRIPTION_ID
az account show --query '{subscription:name,tenant:tenantId}' -o table
steps.expect: The subscription, approved region and required resource IDs are recorded.
steps.notes: These are optional facilitator setup slides, outside the four class hours. Provision the service before session 2. Azure hosting can incur charges. Follow the guide for registry RBAC versus ABAC image-pull roles and outbound access to assigned Zenity endpoints.

steps.title: Lookup image build
steps.where: Clean release extraction > Azure Container Registry
actions: Prepare lookup-build with the files listed in guide section 4.
Build the image and record its digest. Keep secrets outside the build directory.
steps.input:
az acr build --registry YOUR_REGISTRY_NAME \
  --image zenity-remediation-lookup:0.1.0-beta.1 \
  --file Dockerfile.lookup lookup-build
steps.expect: The image builds and the digest identifies the deployed artifact.
steps.notes: Use deploy/standalone/Dockerfile.lookup. Include connector_server.py, engine.py, profiles.py, evidence.py, live_guidance.py, zenity_auth.py, zenity_reader.py, lookup_result.py when present, and profiles/. The current source includes lookup_result.py. Pin the image digest in deployment parameters.

steps.title: Private deployment parameters
steps.where: Template example > private file outside Git
actions: Copy lookup.parameters.example.json to a private location.
Set resource IDs, pinned image, fixed connection values and secret references.
steps.input:
serviceKey: separate random key, at least 32 characters
zenityCredentials: Zenity client ID and client secret
connection: assigned scope, API and OAuth settings
steps.expect: The parameter file stays private and the endpoint values match the assigned environment.
steps.notes: The region field is only a label. Do not derive the API or OAuth endpoint from a geographic guess. Preserve exact issuer and audience values. The template stores connection, credential and service-key values as Container Apps secrets. Never save filled parameters in the training branch.

steps.title: Azure template validation
actions: Review the lookup-service.azure.json template and private parameters.
Validate before creating the deployment.
steps.input:
az deployment group validate \
  --resource-group YOUR_RESOURCE_GROUP \
  --template-file lookup-service.azure.json \
  --parameters @/PRIVATE_PATH/lookup.parameters.local.json
steps.expect: Template validation succeeds for the intended resource group.
steps.notes: Template validation does not prove Zenity authentication or a live lookup. Resolve missing resources, identity assignment or invalid parameter values before continuing.

steps.title: Lookup service deployment
actions: Run deployment group create with the same reviewed template and parameters.
Record the returned hostname and check the running revision.
steps.input:
az deployment group create --resource-group YOUR_RESOURCE_GROUP \
  --template-file lookup-service.azure.json \
  --parameters @/PRIVATE_PATH/lookup.parameters.local.json \
  --query properties.outputs.hostname.value -o tsv
steps.expect: The revision runs and Azure supplies the HTTPS hostname.
steps.notes: Ingress targets container port 8080, and Azure terminates HTTPS. The template keeps one replica running. The root URL need not provide a health page. Complete the anonymous denial and live connector checks after startup.

steps.title: Facilitator rehearsal gate
actions: Complete AZT01 through AZT05 using the planned training versions.
Record safe failure codes and leave every failed or unrun check open.
Prepare a safe recording as a teaching fallback.
steps.expect: The record distinguishes actual live acceptance from offline and recorded demonstrations.
steps.notes: The repository reports rehearsed solution import and Teams channel activation. The API-key Azure recipe and live Teams finding conversation still require target-environment acceptance. Producing this course or merging its files does not establish those outcomes.
